column5: Kodak's 1918 tinting and toning guide lists named tones: TONE A copper red, E sepia, F sulphide, G olive green, H blue iron, I pale blue, plus dye tones J to M. Each tone is a bath recipe with temperature and time. Use the names and the order of the process, not the formulas, which are historical.

Tinting and toning are two processes. Toning changes the silver image; tinting dyes the gelatin. The guide gives dye tinting at 65 degrees F with acetic acid up to 0.05 per cent. A useful distinction for an analog finishing lesson.
Historical caution: the bath times and temperatures are for 1918 positive stock at a set bath strength. The course must say they are historical and must not give them as current instructions.
